What drives us
Our customers ensure reliable, safe, and economic transportation
worldwide. We are proud of this - because we work for everyone
who keeps the world moving. We therefore see ourselves as an
important part of society. This role comes with responsibility:
towards our employees, our customers, and all people affected
by our business activities.


A significant responsibility arises from our mission to offer
solutions for sustainable transport in line with applicable
regulations. Here, we are committed to making a substantial
contribution - fully aware that sustainable transport for society
can succeed only if our customers find the right conditions for
economic activity in their markets. Together with our partners,
we are shaping the technological and service-oriented
advancement of the transport sector, with the ambition
to become the best Company in our industry. This is entirely
in the spirit of our founders and in line with our purpose.


We bring the future to the road -
for all who keep the world moving.

Digital report
For sustainability reasons, annual and interim reports are not printed.
These are made available at w www.daimlertruck.com/en/
investors/reports/financial-reports and are available for download as
a PDF. The report in this PDF format contains interactive elements.
Tables of contents, page headers and internal and external
references are linked to the corresponding content.

Editorial notes
Due to rounding, individual figures may not add up precisely to the
totals shown and percentages presented may not accurately reflect
the absolute values to which they relate. This report is available in
German and English. The German version is binding. For better
readability, names, brands and registered trademarks are not
identified in this report.

Diversity, equal opportunities and inclusion are important to us
For this reason, we use gender-neutral language throughout this
report. In the interest of readability and for terms with legal meaning,
we use the generic masculine form. In these cases, the terms chosen
include all gender identities without limitation.

Terminology
This document contains terms such as “zero-emission (heavy-duty) vehicle” (abbreviated “ZEV”, “zero-emission vehicle”), “CO2e”, “CO2e-neutral”, “CO2e-neutral on the balance sheet” and “locally CO2e-free” or “CO2e-free in driving operation”. A “zero-emission heavy-duty
vehicle” is according to Article 3 point (11) (a) of the Regulation (EU) 2024/1610 a vehicle without an internal combustion engine or with an internal combustion engine with emissions of no more than 3 g CO2/(tkm) or 1 g CO2/(pkm). “CO2e” stands for carbon dioxide
equivalent and refers to the total amount of greenhouse gases released by a particular activity or process. It takes into account not only carbon dioxide, but also other greenhouse gases such as methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O) and ozone (O3) by relating their climate impact
to CO2. Since these gases have different effects on the climate, CO2e enables a holistic view of the climate effect of a particular activity. “CO2e-neutral” means that CO₂e emissions released into the atmosphere by a company’s activities are offset by a corresponding amount of
CO2e. Offsetting can be achieved through various measures: reducing emissions, reducing energy consumption, switching to renewable energies, etc., or by storing or absorbing CO₂. “CO2e-neutral on the balance sheet” means that CO₂e emissions released are offset by
compensation certificates and related projects. “Locally CO2e-free” or “CO2e-free in driving operation” means that no carbon or carbon dioxide equivalents (CO2e) is emitted from the vehicle into the immediate surroundings while driving. Unless otherwise indicated, the same
understanding of terms is used in each case throughout the entire document.

                                                                           added complexity.

                                                                           adjusted return on sales of 7.8 percent in our Industrial Business.

                                                                           Equally important, we continued to successfully position our Company for greater

Report of the
Supervisory Board on
the 2025 Financial Year
Dear Shareholders,
A turbulent year 2025 lies behind us – and we must note: the world has become more
complex and volatile. Circumstances that we have taken for granted for decades are
changing profoundly. The resulting uncertainties fundamentally impact entrepreneurial
activity. Against this backdrop in particular, geopolitics has become a central factor in
strategic corporate management – not only for the global economy as a whole, but
directly for Daimler Truck.

In this challenging environment, the global team under Karin Rådström's leadership
has delivered outstanding work. The generational change in management is proving its
worth. The Company's strategic and operational direction has been consistently
developed with the close involvement of the Supervisory Board. The Company's
transformation is in full swing.

Work in the further committees
The Presidential and Remuneration Committee met five times in
the 2025 financial year and passed two resolutions without holding a
meeting. The Committee's work focused on issues of corporate
governance and Board of Management remuneration, with the latter
being an important focus topic. The Presidential and Remuneration
Committee also supported the Chairman of the Supervisory Board in
his work and dealt with the assumption of external and other
mandates by Board of Management members, personnel matters and
directors’ and officers’ insurance (D&O insurance).

The Nomination Committee met four times in the 2025 financial
year and passed one resolution without holding a meeting. The
subject of its work was the preparation for the elections of
shareholder representatives by the Annual General Meeting for the
2026 financial year and the handling of the aforementioned changes
on the shareholder side during the 2025 financial year. As part of a
comprehensive selection and analysis process, with particular

Objectives and Strategy
In 2025, we have set the strategy to build the best truck and bus company – for our customers, our employees, and our shareholders.

Our purpose                                                               A.04
                                                                          Our strategic framework
Trucks and buses are the backbone of our economy and society. The
world stands still without them. At Daimler Truck, we like to say with
conviction and pride: We work for all who keep the world moving –
for the haulers who transport goods from ports around the world to
supermarkets, construction sites and hospitals. For transport
providers who bring people to work, school or on holiday. For the
public services that keep our streets and cities clean, and for many
more. We work for all who keep the world moving – this is our
purpose and motivates us every single day.

Our ambition

At Daimler Truck, we are driven by a clear ambition: to build the best
truck and bus company - for our customers, our employees, and our
shareholders.

For our customers, our goal is to be their first choice. This means not
only delivering great vehicles but also providing reliable support that
enables their businesses to succeed. For our employees, it means
being an employer of choice - attracting and developing top talent,
fostering engagement, and empowering our people to achieve their
full potential. For our shareholders we aim to create lasting value by
strengthening our resilience, driving volume and revenue growth and
achieving industry leading margins.

For 2030 we are targeting an adjusted return on sales of >12% and
an organic compound annual growth rate of 3-5% for our Industrial
Business revenue.

Opening of the Global Parts Center in Halberstadt
The Daimler Truck Global Parts Center in Halberstadt, Germany, has
begun its phased commissioning. This new Daimler Truck site in the
state of Saxony-Anhalt serves as the central hub for global spare
parts logistics for Mercedes-Benz Trucks, enabling fast and
comprehensive parts supply - a key success factor for Daimler Truck.
The official opening ceremony of the central logistics location took
place on July 10, 2025, in the presence of Dr. Reiner Haseloff, who
was Minister President of Saxony-Anhalt at the time, just two years
after the official groundbreaking ceremony. From the outset, the
Global Parts Center was designed for a balance sheet CO₂e-neutral
operation.

Overall assessment
of the economic situation

The completed 2025 financial year was characterized by ongoing
uncertainty. Nevertheless, global economic growth remained roughly
at the previous year's level, as major economic regions in particular
demonstrated resilient growth. Key central banks reduced interest
rates, thus creating a less restrictive monetary policy environment.
However, the introduction of tariffs led to significant shifts in trade
flows, with the uncertainty giving rise to some negative effects on the
industrial sector and related investments.

Due to uncertainties in the North American market, unit sales in the
Trucks North America segment decreased by 26% to 141,814 units in
2025. The other segments of the Industrial Business were able to
maintain or even slightly increase their unit sales levels compared to
the prior year. Overall, unit sales declined by 8% to 422,510 units.

The Group's adjusted EBIT from continuing and discontinued
operations decreased by 19% to €3.8 billion, primarily due to
declining results in the profitable North American business. Despite
this challenging environment, Daimler Truck achieved the outlook for
unit sales, revenue, and earnings for the 2025 financial year, as
updated in the Q2 2025 interim report – both at the Group level and
in the Industrial Business. The adjusted return on sales of the
Industrial Business from continuing and discontinued operations was
7.8% (2024 : 8.9%). The Financial Services segment increased its
adjusted return on equity to 6.1% (2024: 5.0%) despite a decline in
contract volume.

A comparison of key figures of the outlook with the actual
development in the 2025 financial year as well as the outlook for the
2026 financial year is included in table ä B.116 of Chapter
E Outlook.

B.31
Daimler Truck Code of Conduct


Category                                                  Description
Most important content                                    Our Code of Conduct governs the essential principles for action within the Daimler Truck Group. It covers the following topics, among others: respect for human rights, compliance
                                                          with laws and internal regulations, appropriate behavior within the Daimler Truck Group and towards authorities, officials, business partners and customers, dealing with conflicts of
                                                          interest, prohibition of corruption in any form, protection of company assets, fulfillment of our social and corporate responsibility, handling of data.
General objectives                                        The Daimler Truck Code of Conduct defines which rules apply to all of us and the principles by which we work.
Reference to material impacts, risks or opportunities     The Daimler Truck Code of Conduct forms the backbone of our corporate culture and helps to promote ethical business practices within the Group.
Monitoring process                                        Compliance with our code of conduct is monitored within the framework of standard processes, particularly by management and, among others, by the Compliance and Corporate
                                                          Audit departments.
Scope                                                     This policy applies to all employees, members of the executive bodies of Daimler Truck Holding AG, Daimler Truck AG, and all controlled Group companies. We also expect our
                                                          business partners to familiarize themselves with and adhere to this policy.
Responsible organizational level                          The Compliance department is headed by the Chief Legal and Compliance Officer and reports directly to the President & CEO.
Reference to standards and initiatives of third parties   We respect internationally recognized human rights and base our actions on the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights. We therefore attach particular importance to
                                                          the rights set out in the United Nations Bill of Human Rights and the core labor standards of the International Labor Organization.
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders            We want to work with all employees, (Company) employee representatives, and unions in a respectful and trusting manner. We aim to achieve a fair balance between the economic
                                                          interests of the Company and the interests of the employees.
Availability of the policy for stakeholders               The Code of Conduct is publicly available on the website w www.daimlertruck.com/en/company/compliance/daimler-truck-code-of-conduct and is available to all employees at any
                                                          time via the central policy platform.



B.32
Compliance Master Policy


Category                                                  Description
Most important content                                    This policy governs the implementation of the applicable legal and regulatory requirements and regulations within Daimler Truck Holding AG and its directly or indirectly controlled
                                                          companies.
General objectives                                        The aim is to prevent or minimize compliance and reputational risks as well as damage to Daimler Truck and its employees.
Reference to material impacts, risks or opportunities     The CMS provides a structured framework to promote compliant behavior in all relevant compliance areas and to minimize compliance risks.
Monitoring process                                        The central compliance department reviews the processes and measures for all defined compliance fields and program elements. This review assesses appropriateness,
                                                          implementation, and effectiveness through an annual compliance monitoring process. Corporate Audit independently and on a risk-based basis checks selected compliance fields
                                                          and program elements and their implementation in the controlled Group companies.
Scope                                                     This policy applies worldwide to all employees and members of managing bodies of Daimler Truck Holding AG and all controlled Group companies.
Responsible organizational level                          The Compliance department is headed by the Chief Legal and Compliance Officer and reports directly to the President & CEO.
Reference to standards and initiatives of third parties   The design of the CMS is based on the recognized auditing standard IDW PS 980, which is supplemented in detail by other recognized international standards such as ISO 37301
                                                          and best practices.
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders            When drawing up the policy, the interests of employees, customers, business partners and investors were taken into account.
Availability of the policy for stakeholders               The policy is available to all employees at all times via the central policy platform.

Material impacts, risks and opportunities                                                                                                                                         Category


E1 Climate protection and climate change adaptation
  We offer innovative products and services in the area of alternative drive technologies                                                                                         Positive Impact
  CO₂e emissions (Scope 1, 2, and 3) contribute to global warming                                                                                                                 Negative Impact
  Energy-efficient practices and own generation of renewable energy can lead to cost reductions                                                                                   Chance
  Physical risks can cause production downtime and supply chain disruptions (PHY)                                                                                                 Risk
  Current and new regulations can lead to higher operating costs and liability problems (TRA)                                                                                     Risk
  Disruptive technologies can cause risks in product development and increase research and development (R&D) costs (TRA)                                                          Risk
  The slow development of the infrastructure for alternative drive technologies may limit the unit sales of these vehicles (TRA)                                                  Risk
E2 Prevention of environmental pollution
  The air emissions caused by our vehicles can harm the environment and affect human health                                                                                       Negative Impact
E5 Resource efficiency and circular economy
  Considering resource efficiency in vehicle development and design promotes waste prevention and reduction                                                                       Positive Impact
  The production of vehicles leads to a high consumption of raw materials such as iron, steel, aluminum and other materials                                                       Negative Impact
  Non-compliance with circular economy regulations and requirements can lead to risks for our Company                                                                             Risk

B.36
Master Policy Environmental Protection


Category                                                                Description
Most important content                                                  For Daimler Truck, environmental protection means being active in the following areas: climate protection, climate change adaptation, resource preservation, energy efficiency,
                                                                        prevention of environmental pollution, water, waste, energy, and hazardous substances management. Contribution to the circular economy and biodiversity is also of importance
                                                                        to the Group. This policy contains the environmental guidelines as an expression of the environmental policy of the Daimler Truck Group and forms the framework for the
                                                                        environmental and energy management systems:
                                                                        1. We face future challenges in the environmental sector head-on
                                                                        2. We develop products that are environmentally friendly throughout their entire life cycle and contribute to sustainable transport
                                                                        3. We continuously reduce the environmental impact of our operations and strive for clean and environmentally friendly production
                                                                        4. We offer our customers comprehensive service and information on the environmental life cycle of our products
                                                                        5. We aim to provide exemplary environmental performance worldwide
                                                                        6. We provide our employees and stakeholders with comprehensive information about our environmental performance and specific commitments
                                                                        To further specify this, we have implemented the subordinate expert policy on climate protection. This contains not only climate-related decarbonization targets and planned key
                                                                        lever, but also information on how Daimler Truck is responding to physical and transitional climate risks in order to strengthen its resilience to climate change.
General objectives                                                      The aim of the Group-wide policy is to provide a foundation for Daimler Truck Group's environmental protection and principles of action. In this context, environmental protection
                                                                        and the pursuit of greenhouse gas emission neutrality are an integral part of the corporate strategy, which is aimed at long-term value creation. The goal of enabling locally CO₂e-
                                                                        free transport on the roads includes careful handling of natural resources. Furthermore, the aim of the expert guideline on climate protection is to create a framework that
                                                                        focuses on climate protection actions and integrates climate protection as an integral part into core business processes.
Reference to material impacts, risks, or opportunities                  Our Corporate Environmental Protection Policy contains guidelines on the material impacts, risks, and opportunities related to climate protection and climate change adaptation,
                                                                        as described in ä B.35.
Monitoring process                                                      Compliance with environmental guidelines at production sites is monitored within the framework of our existing environmental and energy management systems, including ISO
                                                                        14001/ ISO 50001, EMAS, and environmental risk audits.
Scope                                                                   The policy applies to all employees and managing body members of Daimler Truck Holding AG, as well as all controlled Group companies.
Responsible organizational level                                        Our environmental policy, including the guidelines, must be applied by all employees of the Daimler Truck Group and at all of the Group's locations. Managers at all levels bear
                                                                        particular responsibility in this regard.
Reference to Third-Party Standards and Initiatives                      Based on the Company-wide environmental guidelines, Daimler Truck requires its production sites worldwide to implement management systems certified according to ISO
                                                                        14001 and ISO 50001. ISO stands for the International Organization for Standardization, whose standards help companies to implement uniform and recognized practices
                                                                        worldwide. In addition, our sites in Germany are required to be certified according to EMAS.
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders                          The interests of the Group’s employees, customers, suppliers, contractual partners, associations and authorities, public initiatives, other stakeholders, and the public are taken
                                                                        into account in the policy.
Availability of the policy for stakeholders                             All master policies are available to all employees at any time via the central policy platform. The environmental guidelines are also made available on the Group's public website.

                                                                           Governance structure and responsibility
For the production sites in Europe, we use a calculation
tool to obtain transparency about CO₂e emissions based on real
transport data and thus measure the effect of optimization actions or,
e.g., the use of battery electric trucks. The calculation logic was
certified by the Smart Freight Center in 2023 and complies with the
standard of the Global Logistics Emissions Council (GLEC). In 2024,
we rolled out this calculation tool globally in order to record the CO₂e
emissions of global transports in a standardized manner. With the
development of the data model for the organizational units Daimler
Truck North America, Daimler India Commercial Vehicles, and
Mitsubishi Fuso Truck and Bus Corporation, we now have a nearly
complete picture of the transport of production materials. In 2025,
the last gaps, as with Mercedes-Benz do Brasil Ltd., were closed, the
annual data update was carried out, and the GLEC certification was
extended to include the new scopes.

B.50
Ecodesign Guideline


Category                                                                Description
Key Content                                                             As part of our Ecodesign Guideline, we have established a structured process for implementing and managing ecodesign in vehicle development, taking into account ecodesign
                                                                        guidelines and assessment procedures. With this holistic approach to vehicle development (part of the Creation Phase) ecological aspects are systematically and bindingly
                                                                        considered in all phases of product development. A key element is the systematic preparation of design specifications and recommendations for the targeted use of more
                                                                        sustainable materials and construction principles – focusing, among other things, on ease of disassembly, complexity reduction, component consolidation, and weight optimization.
                                                                        Best-practice examples and flagship projects serve as guidance and inspiration for further projects, supporting development teams. A key element of the ecodesign process is the
                                                                        application of defined methods for reducing the CO₂e footprint and to promote circular economy throughout the entire product life cycle. These include, e.g., the selection of durable,
                                                                        resource-efficient and recyclable materials and the execution of life cycle analyses, and considering reusability, repairability and recyclability in existing material cycles. Ecodesign
                                                                        principles should thus be applied in all relevant decision-making and approval processes during vehicle development.
General Objectives                                                      The Ecodesign Guideline aims to embed the integration of ecodesign into our development processes. Its goal is to reduce the environmental impact of our products throughout their
                                                                        entire life cycle, increase resource efficiency and durability, and promote the use of circular materials. Rooted in the principles of circular economy, it supports the development of
                                                                        products, components, and materials designed from the outset for reuse, repair, remanufacturing, and recycling. At the same time, production and logistics processes are to be
                                                                        improved to avoid waste, close material loops, and embed sustainable solutions throughout the entire value chain.
Relation to Material Impacts, Risks or Opportunities                    The Ecodesign Guideline addresses the impacts described in Table ä B.49 in connection with resource efficiency and circular economy.
Monitoring Process                                                      The application of ecodesign is monitored by defining responsibilities.
Scope                                                                   The Ecodesign Guideline is applied in the Mercedes-Benz Trucks and Daimler Buses segments.
Responsible Organizational Level                                        The Ecodesign Guideline must be applied by developers in the relevant areas. The heads of product development at Mercedes-Benz Trucks and Daimler Buses bear ultimate
                                                                        responsibility for this.
Reference to Third-Party Standards and Initiatives                      Our lifecycle assessments take into account the requirements of ISO 14040.
Consideration of the Interests of Stakeholders                          The interests of the Group's employees, customers, associations and authorities, as well as other stakeholders , are taken into account in the Ecodesign Guideline.
Availability of the Policy for Stakeholders                             The Ecodesign Guideline is made available to all employees via the social intranet and, in the future, via BIC Cloud.

                                                                                          B.53
                                                                                          Circular economy




We are committed to reducing waste in production. By 2030, the sum
of all effects should achieve an annual reduction of 41 kt compared
to the base year.1 Our Master Policy Environmental Protection
contains provisions for reducing waste generation. We adhere to the
five-step waste hierarchy regulated in Section 6 of the German
Circular Economy Act (KrWG). Waste prevention is the primary
objective, followed by preparing materials for reuse, recycling, and
other recovery processes. To account for the different production
sites and their associated specific characteristics, these were
involved in setting the waste target, and variable influencing factors
were considered in addition to a fixed reduction. Specific scientific
frameworks were not taken into account in setting the target.

Currently, no reliable industry data is available for comparing the
durability of our products (truck and buses). Based on internal
information and assessments, we can assume that the durability of
our products is in line with the industry average. This internal
information is based on customer feedback regarding mileage, usage,
and repair frequency. While this feedback is valuable, it still has some
limitations, as it is not collected comprehensively for all vehicles.

The spare parts determination begins in the product development
phase. Interdisciplinary teams from development, marketing,
aftersales and supplier management work out potential repair
concepts. Important criteria include avoiding scrapping parts,
serviceability, cost-effectiveness and reusability of the spare parts.
Based on design groups into which the entire vehicle is divided, we
analyze all assemblies in order to determine the optimal repair
strategy. If a repair is technically possible, the components, such as
complete mirrors, engine components, and seats, are divided into
substructures (individual part numbers to be ordered) and the repair
depth is determined. The repair depth indicates how far we can
disassemble an assembly into individual parts.

For a complete seat, e.g., this means that we can replace or repair
components such as armrests, backrests and seat covers separately.
Another input factor for the definition of spare parts is the product
testing work, which deals with vehicles already in use.
We analyze complaints to understand the actual causes of damage
and define appropriate repair solutions and parts kits.
This means that we can selectively replace the damaged components
and do not have to replace the entire assembly.

Therefore, we are constantly working both preventively in the product
development process and reactively in the product validation process
to improve our spare parts range and align it with environmental and
customer-oriented needs. With the ongoing development of the
product portfolio, repairs can be offered not only for conventional
components, but also for complex electrical components, such as the
high-voltage battery. As part of repairs, individual parts that were not
affected by a defect can generally be reused.

B.61
Declaration of Principles on Social Responsibility and Human Rights at Daimler Truck


Category                                                                               Description
Most important content                                                                 In the Declaration of Principles, we acknowledge our social responsibility and summarize our commitment to respect human rights. The Declaration of Principles supplements our
                                                                                       commitment under the Daimler Truck Code of Conduct and describes the approach, processes and measures to respect human rights at Daimler Truck.
                                                                                       It is based on international standards such as the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights. Important content includes:
                                                                                        – Commitment to human rights and good working conditions, in particular:
                                                                                                 •     Rejection of child labor, forced labor and human trafficking, and commitment to their effective abolition
                                                                                                 •     Promoting equal opportunities and rejecting any kind of discrimination
                                                                                                 •     Commitment to the protection of health and safety at work
                                                                                                 •     Promoting education and training for all employees
                                                                                           –    Description of our Human Rights Compliance Management System, our systematic approach to fulfilling human rights due diligence obligations
                                                                                           –    Governance and responsibilities for implementation and monitoring of the Declaration of Principles
                                                                                           –    Access to redress human rights violations and our whistleblowing system SpeakUp
General objectives                                                                     The general objective is to reinforce our commitment to social responsibility and respect for human rights. It serves as the basis for our activities in the field of human rights and
                                                                                       provides clear guidance to both internal and external stakeholders, especially our employees.
Reference to material impacts, risks, or opportunities                                 Preventing discrimination and human rights violations, thereby reducing reputational and financial risks.
Monitoring process                                                                     The risk management for fulfilling human rights due diligence obligations - as described in the policy statement - is monitored by the Daimler Truck Group's human rights officer. In
                                                                                       addition, employees and external third parties worldwide can report potential human rights violations via the channels of our whistleblowing system SpeakUp.
Scope                                                                                  This regulation applies to all employees and members of the managing bodies of Daimler Truck Holding AG and all controlled Group companies.
Responsible organizational level                                                       The members of Daimler Truck's executive bodies are responsible for implementing the policy statement. Local implementation is the responsibility of the managers at each location.
                                                                                       The Legal & Compliance department of Daimler Truck AG, reporting directly to the President & CEO, is responsible for all overarching human rights activities. This department works
                                                                                       closely with the specialist departments responsible for the operational implementation of human rights due diligence within the Group – in particular, Human Resources and
                                                                                       Procurement.
Reference to standards and initiatives of third parties                                In this context, we commit ourselves, among others, to respecting the following international standards: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, International Covenant on Civil and
                                                                                       Political Rights, International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work, UN Guiding Principles on Business
                                                                                       and Human Rights, 10 Principles of the UN Global Compact, and OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises.
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders                                         The Declaration of Principles was agreed and adopted by the Board of Management together with the general works council, the global employee representation of Daimler Truck
                                                                                       and the international trade union association industriAll Global Union in November 2022.
Availability of the policy for stakeholders                                            The Declaration of Principles is available in more than ten languages on the Daimler Truck Group website at w www.daimlertruck.com/en/sustainability/people/human-rights/
                                                                                       declaration-of-principles. The Daimler Truck Group employees were also informed of the Declaration of Principles via various internal communication channels, e.g. via the
                                                                                       company's own intranet. Our suppliers can also access the policy statement via the Daimler Truck Supplier Portal and were also informed of its adoption there.

Through our business model, we focus in particular on two groups of
employees: our employees in production and our employees in
administration. In principle, we do not differentiate between these
groups when evaluating material impacts, risks, and opportunities.
However, due to the transformation of our products and drive
technologies, measures naturally differ, e.g. in occupational safety,
retraining, training, and the recruitment of skilled workers.

HR compliance
The Human Resources Compliance Management System (HR CMS)
defines the framework and provides tools for legally compliant, non-
discriminatory, and ethically responsible HR practices across the
entire Daimler Truck Group. In line with Daimler Truck's corporate
values, the HR Compliance Master Policy establishes binding
principles and requirements for implementing legal requirements,
regulatory standards, and Group-wide self-commitments and ethical
principles.

B.70
Rule Violation and Investigation Master Policy


Category                                                  Description
Most important content                                    This policy aims to provide transparent handling of reported misconduct – from reporting a potential violation to investigation and possible follow-up measures. It is also intended to
                                                          ensure that the reported circumstances are clarified effectively, transparently and in accordance with the law, taking into account the rights and obligations of all parties involved.
General objectives                                        This policy is intended to protect the safety and security of the Daimler Truck Group, its employees, its contractual and business partners, and external third parties. It aims to
                                                          ensure effective, transparent, and fundamental rights-compliant investigations into violations of applicable laws and Daimler Truck Group rules. The procedure outlines the SpeakUp
                                                          procedure and the responsibilities of the various parties involved. It also defines the criteria for assessing and the consequences of rule violations.
Reference to material impacts, risks, or opportunities    The policy creates a safe environment for reporting discrimination and other human rights violations by defining clear reporting channels, safeguards, and transparent investigation
                                                          procedures. This allows these and other legal infringements to be identified and investigated early on, preventing harm to Daimler Truck and its employees and ensuring fair
                                                          cooperation. It also mitigates reputational and financial risks.
Monitoring process                                        Compliance with our Rule Violation and Investigation Master Policy is monitored within the framework of standard processes, particularly by management and, among others, by the
                                                          Compliance and Corporate Audit departments.
Scope                                                     All Daimler Truck Group companies.
Responsible organizational level                          The Compliance department under the direction of the Chief Legal and Compliance Officer with a direct reporting line to the President & CEO.
Reference to standards and initiatives of third parties   The policy complies with legal requirements, e.g., from the German Whistleblower Protection Act.
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders            The policy takes the interests of those affected into account in the procedure. The revision of these regulations, which are subject to co-determination in Germany, was carried out in
                                                          close coordination and intensive exchange between the responsible departments (Legal, Compliance, Corporate Audit, and HR), the Group Works Council and the Group
                                                          Spokespersons' Committee.
Availability of the policy for stakeholders               The policy is available to all employees at all times via the central policy platform.

B.71
HR Compliance Master Policy


Category                                                  Description
Most important content                                    The policy establishes binding standards Group-wide for legally compliant, non-discriminatory, and ethically responsible HR practices. It contains clear guidelines for compliance with
                                                          labor law and human rights due diligence obligations, as well as data protection. Key principles of internal control, such as the four-eyes principle and the mandatory, traceable
                                                          documentation of relevant HR processes, are integral parts of the policy. Continuous monitoring and ongoing development of these measures strengthen compliance within HR.
General objectives                                        This policy establishes clear responsibilities, principles, and standards for compliant and ethically responsible HR management within the Group. It ensures adherence to
                                                          international and national regulations, promotes equal opportunities and fair treatment, and guarantees high labor and social standards for the workforce. Monitoring and continuous
                                                          improvement tools strengthen compliance and support a culture of trust within the Company, as well as effective risk minimization in HR.
Reference to material impacts, risks, or opportunities    The policy addresses material impacts, risks, and opportunities related to the Company's workforce. It promotes equal opportunities, supports protection against discrimination,
                                                          contributes to respect for human rights, and establishes clear, legally compliant, and fair working conditions for employees. Binding standards for HR management, occupational
                                                          health and safety, and training measures proactively minimize risks such as work overload, lack of professional development, unequal treatment, and legal violations. At the same
                                                          time, the policy helps foster a responsible corporate culture and strengthen the Company's competitiveness.
Monitoring process                                        The monitoring process involves the ongoing, systematic review and measurement of compliance with defined standards across all relevant Companies. The insights gained are used
                                                          to continuously improve HR processes and compliance measures.
Scope                                                     This policy applies to all employees and members of managing bodies of Daimler Truck Holding AG and all controlled Group companies.
Responsible organizational level                          Overall responsibility for the implementation and adherence to this policy lies with HR top managers and the respective HR departments in all relevant Companies. They are
                                                          specifically responsible for designing, implementing, and continuously conducting internal controls and compliance measures, as well as promoting good working conditions. The
                                                          executive management creates the necessary framework for compliance with the policy and contributes to integrity and a values-based approach ("Tone from the Top") through
                                                          exemplary conduct.
Reference to standards and initiatives of third parties   The policy is based on the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, the International Bill of Human Rights, the fundamental conventions of the ILO, and the UN Global
                                                          Compact. It also provides a sound basis for HR-related reporting obligations in accordance with the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), the European Sustainability
                                                          Reporting Standard S1 (ESRS S1), and the German Supply Chain Due Diligence Act.
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders            The development of the HR Compliance Master Policy incorporated the perspectives and expectations of key stakeholders such as employees, managers, executives, and employee
                                                          representatives. This ensures that the policy is practical and reflects the requirements of all essential stakeholders.
Availability of the policy for stakeholders               The policy is available to all employees at all times via the central policy platform.

B.75
Master Policy on Occupational Health and Safety


Category                                                                Description
Most important content                                                  This policy defines the responsibilities and objectives in occupational health and safety. It outlines essential and generally applicable requirements for the structure of the
                                                                        occupational health and safety organization and regulations for legally compliant planning and safe operation in the Daimler Truck Group.
General objectives                                                      Our goal is to protect the occupational safety and health of all employees, identify and prevent health risks and hazards, and at the same time promote well-being as a prerequisite
                                                                        for creativity and productivity.
Reference to material impacts, risks, or opportunities                  In our opinion, the policy can prevent accident and health risks, which also reduces reputational and financial risks and increases productivity.
Monitoring process                                                      In our annual employee survey, two questions are devoted to the topics of occupational safety, health and well-being in order to obtain a Company-wide mood picture. The key topics
                                                                        of occupational safety and health protection are also regularly discussed, evaluated and further developed with various internal committees, such as the Commission for
                                                                        Occupational Safety, Environment and Health, as well as with works council and Company representatives at all Company levels and with external committees such as the Company
                                                                        health insurance fund's administrative board. In addition, the positive effects of the measures are incorporated into the exchange with managers and employees.
Scope                                                                   This policy applies to all employees and members of managing bodies of Daimler Truck Holding AG and all controlled Group companies.
Responsible organizational level                                        The highest level of the organization responsible for developing and monitoring the implementation of the policy is Corporate Health and Safety.
Reference to standards and initiatives of third parties                 We are committed to "Vision Zero" and are part of a global initiative by the Institution of Occupational Safety and Health (IOSH) and the International Social Security Association
                                                                        (ISSA) that aims to prevent work-related accidents and illnesses while promoting the safety, health and well-being of employees.
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders                          When drawing up this policy, we have taken into account the interests of all relevant stakeholders to ensure a safe and healthy working environment. These include, e.g. employees,
                                                                        executives and management, and the works council.
Availability of the policy for stakeholders                             The policy is available to all employees at all times via the central policy platform.

B.78
Global Compensation Master Policy


Category                                                              Description
Most important content                                                The Global Compensation Master Policy sets out the framework and minimum requirements for the design of compensation systems. We strive to compensate for work performed in
                                                                      all Group companies worldwide according to the same principles. Among other things, it stipulates that the level of compensation is based on the assigned requirements of the job -
                                                                      taking into account, among other things, knowledge, skills, responsibility and decision-making authority - and the person's performance, not gender, origin or other personal
                                                                      characteristics. It defines the remuneration components, the standards and framework conditions to be observed, as well as the approval regulations, documentation, and retention
                                                                      obligations.
General objectives                                                    The aim of this policy is to create a framework for remuneration issues within the Daimler Truck Group.
Reference to material impacts, risks, or opportunities                In our opinion, the policy can prevent discrimination and violations of human rights, which also reduces reputational and financial risks.
Monitoring process                                                    Internal audits are carried out annually by the internal audit department on a random basis to check whether selected aspects of the policy are being complied with. We also take the
                                                                      conditions of the local markets into account, as we want to offer our employees salaries and additional benefits in line with the market.
Scope                                                                 It applies to Daimler Truck Holding AG, Daimler Truck AG, and all controlled Group companies. In addition to all HR employees within the Daimler Truck Group, the policy is valid for
                                                                      all managers in executive positions at controlled Group companies who are responsible for the design or restructuring of remuneration systems or the implementation of
                                                                      remuneration processes.
Responsible organizational level                                      The TH OpCom, as the highest decision-making body in the HR department, exercises the authority to issue policies for specifying the remuneration principles established by the
                                                                      Board of Management of Daimler Truck AG and makes decisions on their implementation.
Reference to standards and initiatives of third parties               n/a
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders                        The Global Compensation Master Policy was drawn up by the central compensation policy department in consultation with various central and local HR departments and experts
                                                                      from Legal & Compliance, Corporate Audit and Finance. Changes are approved by the Board of Management. Trade unions and employee representatives are involved in the changes
                                                                      so that the interests of employees are taken into account.
Availability of the policy for stakeholders                           The policy is available to all employees at all times via the central policy platform.

B.81
Supplier Compliance Due Diligence Expert Policy


Category                                                                   Description
Most important content                                                     Supplier Compliance Due Diligence is an internal expert policy that governs the purpose and process of supplier due diligence. At Daimler Truck, the Supplier Compliance Due
                                                                           Diligence ensures a comprehensive risk assessment covering relevant compliance areas in collaboration with suppliers. Respect for human rights and environmental standards, as
                                                                           well as adherence to anti-corruption requirements and related regulations, are top priorities in this expert policy and the corresponding processes and activities.
General objectives                                                         Through an annual risk assessment of all direct suppliers, with substantiated knowledge of (potential) violations, also for indirect suppliers, of the Daimler Truck Group and the Group
                                                                           companies, potential risks in the supply chain are to be identified in order to be effectively addressed through preventive measures.
Reference to material impacts, risks or opportunities                      The focus of the policy is on identifying and prioritizing potential risks. By identifying potential risks early, they can be specifically remedied or minimized.
Monitoring process                                                         Supplier due diligence consists of supplier risk assessment and consequence management, which must be carried out, reviewed and approved by the respective purchasing function.
                                                                           Sanctions screening of all suppliers is ensured by a further process in accordance with the Compliance Policy - Compliance with Sanctions.
Scope                                                                      This expert policy applies to management bodies, all employees and the respective heads of the purchasing functions at Daimler Truck AG, its Group companies, including the
                                                                           employees and the respective heads of the legal and compliance departments who support processes and activities for supplier compliance due diligence.
Responsible organizational level                                           The purchasing departments are primarily responsible for carrying out supplier due diligence. The compliance program department provides the IT system and is the area responsible
                                                                           for the guidelines.
Reference to standards and initiatives of third parties                    Regulations on compliance with due diligence standards under the Supply Chain Due Diligence Act and the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA).
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders                             The Supplier Compliance Due Diligence Expert Policy was developed in consultation with various central and local purchasing departments and experts from Legal, Compliance, and
                                                                           Corporate Audit. This ensures that the policy is practical and reflects the requirements of all key stakeholders.
Availability of the policy for stakeholders                                The policy is available to all employees at all times via the central policy platform.

In addition to environmental aspects, social criteria such as the
existence of management systems to respect human rights, effective
occupational safety measures, responsible raw material procurement
and sustainability-oriented supplier management are included in an
overall assessment, from which the sustainability rating of a supplier
is derived. In the reporting year, 76.2%1 of the planned procurement
volume for 2025 in production material procurement was sourced
from suppliers who have a sustainability rating based on the SAQ.

In the reporting year, we continued to be involved in the "Responsible
Trucking Initiative" within the framework of CSR Europe. Together
with other companies, we are committed to improving the social
conditions of truck drivers in the road transport and logistics sector,
e.g., by recognizing common social guidelines.

We are also a member of the Responsible Supply Chain Initiative e.V.
(RSCI), which offers standardized sustainability audits to evaluate the
implementation of social and environmental standards in automotive
supply chains. We use the RSCI audit program for high-risk suppliers
and suspected cases to create further transparency among suppliers
and to initiate improvements in the future if necessary. In the
reporting year, several audits were carried out at suppliers
internationally.

In addition to our ongoing commitment in various initiatives we are
also involved in the development of an industry-wide escalation
platform within the "Human Rights Working Group" of Drive
Sustainability. This platform is intended to handle suspected cases
involving shared suppliers (the Grievance Escalation Platform). The
goal is to coordinate the processing of complaints, establish
standardized procedures across the industry, and use a central case
database to identify systemic risks in the supply chain at an early
stage and promote continuous improvement. Implementation of this
concept is planned for 2026.

B.83
Product Compliance Management System Policy


Category                                                                  Description
Most important content                                                    This PCMS policy describes the core elements of the product-related Compliance Management System implemented by the Board of Management of the Daimler Truck Group to
                                                                          ensure the regulatory compliance of our products throughout the product life cycle.
General objectives                                                        The aim of the PCMS is to ensure the regulatory compliance of our products, also with regard to product safety and liability requirements, throughout the entire product life cycle
                                                                          (product development, production, sales and use by the customer up to decommissioning).
Reference to material impacts, risks or opportunities                     The policy is designed to ensure the regulatory compliance of our products.
Monitoring process                                                        A monitoring process of the PCMS takes place on an annual basis to evaluate the design, implementation and effectiveness of the PCMS. Appropriate improvements are
                                                                          implemented based on the analysis.
Scope                                                                     The policy applies to all Group companies with the exception of Daimler Truck Financial Services.
Responsible organizational level                                          The implementation of the policy is the responsibility of the relevant business units.
Reference to standards and initiatives of third parties                   To minimize potential product risks, the applicable market-specific product-related laws, regulations, policies, automotive standards or other relevant specifications (e.g., ISO
                                                                          standards, product-related material conformity, technical instructions), in particular with regard to applicable technical requirements have to be observed and complied. The PCMS
                                                                          creates the structures and processes to support this.
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders                            n/a
Availability of the policy for stakeholders                               The policy is available to all employees at all times via the central policy platform.

shown in graphic ä B.84.

Our active safety systems support drivers in carrying out their driving
tasks and can thereby help prevent accidents or reduce their
severity. With these systems, our aim is to increase the driver´s
attention, prevent fatigue, and encourage an adapted driving style,
e.g., through prediction, automation, traffic sign recognition,
improved all-round view, and intelligent light control.

Autonomous driving
We also continued to advance the positive impacts that autonomous
driving can have in the future during the reporting year. Together with
Torc Robotics, we selected Innoviz as a supplier of high-performance
LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) systems for short ranges.
Innoviz is working closely with us on sensor development and is
specifically adapting the technology for commercial applications of
heavy trucks. The plan is to install the InnovizTwo short-range LiDAR
sensors in the Freightliner Cascadia, which will initially be used for
long-haul transport in the USA. Combined with Torc's virtual driving
software, this creates a sensor system that integrates radar, camera,     control units capable of processing large volumes of data. This            Another important part of our work is providing targeted information

                                                                            The Daimler Truck compliance training program

In the event of corruption, we have clearly defined reporting and
escalation processes in place, and the results are made available to
the relevant committees. The compliance organization plays an
advisory and coordinating role, supporting the Board of Management
in complying with legal regulations and requirements. It also lays the
foundation for compliance standards, processes, and culture within
the Daimler Truck Group.

Metrics
During the reporting year, no convictions (2024: 0) or fines (2024: 0)
related to violations of anti-corruption or anti-bribery laws and
regulations were recorded.

Actions
We offer a comprehensive range of training courses on compliance
topics. The need for the training courses is regularly determined and
the content is adapted and further developed in line with the latest
findings. We assign the relevant training modules to employees when
they are hired, promoted or when they change to a higher-risk
position. The web-based training courses are available worldwide via
a Learning Management System. Our administrative staff are
required to attend Code of Conduct training every three years. This
training covers, among other things, the principles of the Daimler
Truck Code of Conduct and our Purpose Principles. It also covers the
correct handling of donations, antitrust law, corruption prevention,

B.89
Daimler Truck Business Partner Standards


Category                                                               Description
Most important content                                                 Our expectations of business partners - including suppliers - regarding respect and protection of human rights, environmental, climate protection, and other compliance-relevant
                                                                       topics are defined in our Daimler Truck Business Partner Standards. This includes in particular the topics of fair wages and occupational safety, respect for freedom of association,
                                                                       requirements for the deployment of security forces, human trafficking, forced and child labor, and responsible use of natural resources.
General objectives                                                     The Daimler Truck Business Partner Standards are intended to ensure that all of the Company's business partners adhere to certain ethical and legal standards in order to protect the
                                                                       Company and its partners from legal and reputational risks. By setting clear standards and expectations regarding respect for human rights, negative impacts on workers in the value
                                                                       chain are prevented.
Reference to material impacts, risks or opportunities                  The Daimler Truck Business Partner Standards are part of Daimler Trucks' strategy for managing its material impacts on workers in the value chain. By formulating our expectations
                                                                       for sustainable action, we make a positive contribution to sustainable business in close cooperation with our business partners, especially suppliers.
Monitoring process                                                     The Business Partner Standards are reviewed as part of the annual measurement of the adequacy, implementation and effectiveness of the CMS.
Scope                                                                  The Daimler Truck Business Partner Standards cover workers in the value chain and do not refer exclusively to specific groups.
Responsible organizational level                                       The Business Partner Standards are created jointly by all relevant Centers of Competence (CoC) from Legal & Compliance as well as relevant specialist departments of Daimler Truck
                                                                       AG.
Reference to standards and initiatives of third parties                In our Business Partner Standards we refer in particular to respect for the following international standards: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, International Covenant on Civil
                                                                       and Political Rights, International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, the core labor standards of the International Labor Organization (ILO), the UN Guiding Principles
                                                                       on Business and Human Rights, and the 10 Principles of the United Nations Global Compact.
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders                         The Business Partner Standards take into account the interests of the relevant stakeholders, in particular our suppliers, service providers and other business partners.
Availability of the policy for stakeholders                            The Business Partner Standards are publicly available on the website w supplier.daimlertruck.com/en/support/news/the-daimler-truck-business-partner-standards and are available
                                                                       to all employees at any time via the central policy platform.

B.90
Mandatory contractual clauses on social responsibility and environmental protection


Category                                                                              Description
Most important content                                                                The clauses define the standards and requirements for suppliers with regard to respect for human rights and good working conditions as well as environmental protection. This
                                                                                      includes in particular the topics of fair wages and occupational safety, respect for freedom of association, requirements for the use of security forces, forced labor and the
                                                                                      responsible use of natural resources. With regard to environmental standards and environmental compatibility, binding specifications for environmentally friendly production, energy
                                                                                      and resource preservation, waste reduction, and chemical management are formulated. In addition, we encourage our suppliers to support our goals with regard to achieving CO₂e
                                                                                      neutrality for our products and services.
General objectives                                                                    The Group-wide binding clauses on social responsibility and environmental protection define clear standards and requirements for cooperation with suppliers. They also ensure the
                                                                                      contractual implementation of the relevant human rights and environmental standards that are expressed in our Business Partner Standards for suppliers. The contractual
                                                                                      arrangement makes it possible to legally enforce our expectations towards suppliers if necessary. It serves both to ensure compliance with legal requirements and to promote social
                                                                                      and environmental standards along the upstream value chain.
Reference to material impacts, risks or opportunities                                 The clauses address the reduction of environmental and climate impacts in the value chain and the minimization of risks through environmentally friendly production processes and
                                                                                      forward-looking resource planning. In addition, they represent an essential component in ensuring that human rights standards are respected at Daimler Truck along our value chain.
                                                                                      Overall, this contributes to the prevention and minimization of negative impacts on workers in the upstream value chain.
Monitoring process                                                                    Monitoring compliance through supplier audits and/or supplier self-assessments; certification audit for environmental management systems according to ISO 14001, EMAS or
                                                                                      comparable standards.
Scope                                                                                 Global requirements for suppliers of production and non-production materials.
Responsible organizational level                                                      The purchasing department is primarily responsible for the effective integration of contractual clauses in our contracts with business partners. It is supported by the legal department
                                                                                      if necessary.
Reference to third-party initiatives                                                  The clauses are based on international standards such as the International Bill of Human Rights and the 10 Principles of the United Nations Global Compact, the United Nations
                                                                                      Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and the International Labour Organization's core labor standards. They also
                                                                                      refer to ISO 14001, EMAS and comparable environmental management standards.
Consideration of the interests of stakeholders                                        Requirements for resource-saving and environmentally friendly production that meet the expectations of environmental initiatives, legal regulations and customer needs.
Availability of the policy for stakeholders                                           The clauses are an integral part of the supplier contracts and are also publicly accessible via the Daimler Truck Supplier Portal at w supplier.daimlertruck.com/en/.

that make a person suitable for a Board of Management position
include, in particular, the individual’s personality, integrity, convincing
leadership qualities, expertise for the segment he or she will head,
previous achievements, knowledge of the Company, and the ability to
adapt business models and processes in a changing world.

Together with the Board of Management, the Supervisory Board also
ensures a long-term succession planning for the Board of
Management, for which it takes the overall requirements profile and
the individual circumstances into account. In this process, it is to
discuss the duration of the contracts of current Board of
Management members, the possibility of extending them, and
potential successors. The duties of the Presidential and
Remuneration Committee of the Supervisory Board also include
holding discussions about the Group’s talented and exceptional
executives at regular intervals. Executives at the management level
below the Board of Management and persons of especially high
potential are to be evaluated on the basis of an analysis of potential
and the criteria of the overall requirements profile, and the next
development steps are then to be discussed and defined together
with the Board of Management. The succession planning process also
includes a regular report from the Board of Management regarding
the proportion and development of female executives. The Board of
Management has the task of recommending a sufficient number of
suitable candidates to the Supervisory Board. The Supervisory Board
aims to primarily fill Board of Management positions with executives
that have risen within the Group. Nonetheless, potential external
candidates may also be evaluated and included in the selection
process, if necessary with the support of external human resources
consulting services.

Risk and Opportunity Report
Daimler Truck is exposed to a variety of risks and opportunities
resulting from both its own business activities and external factors.

To identify, assess, and manage risks and opportunities at an early
stage, the Daimler Truck Group uses management and control
systems, which are consolidated in its risk and opportunity
management system. This system serves to protect company assets,
ensure economic stability, and strengthen resilience. Simultaneously,
it helps to identify and exploit opportunities at an early stage to gain
a competitive advantage and increase business success. The focus is
on the systematic and continuous identification of risks that threaten
the Company's existence and other significant risks that could
jeopardize its success, as well as appropriate risk mitigation
measures. Integrating the risk and opportunity management system
into all business processes ensures a holistic perspective and
supports risk-based decisions at all levels.

The structure and content of the risk and opportunity report was
revised for the reporting period. This is intended to focus the
reporting more strongly on the key risks and opportunities and to
better meet the information needs of stakeholders.
